title: KOSPI plunges 3.65% despite Samsung's record earnings
source_used: The Korea Times (Yonhap photo); read in full via fulltext
key_facts: KOSPI closed at 6,384.24 on Monday 12 Oct 2026, down 241.69 points or 3.65 percent, its fourth straight losing session.
It was the biggest daily percentage fall since 2 Sep, when the index fell 3.99 percent.
The index has lost 619.50 points, or 8.85 percent, since 6 Oct, after losing the 7,000 mark earlier in that stretch.
Samsung Electronics fell 4.39 percent and SK hynix 4.52 percent; persistent foreign selling weighed on the index.

Samsung reported record earnings last Thursday; analysts say solid earnings alone may no longer satisfy investors, who want proof the chip upswing will last and clearer evidence in high-bandwidth memory.

Mirae Asset Securities analyst Kim Seok-hwan linked the fall to renewed AI bubble worries after reports about OpenAI; the Korea Times says the $20 billion revenue gap in those reports reflected different accounting methods, not a drop in sales, so it does not fully explain the weakness.
Kosdaq, the tech-heavy market, fell 4.83 percent to 849.19; the won strengthened to 1,335.1 per dollar.
Coming dates: ASML and TSMC report this week, SK hynix on 27 Oct, Samsung conference call on 29 Oct.
quote_evidence: KOSPI slid 3.65 percent Monday, falling below 6,400 as its losing streak stretched to four consecutive sessions.
Samsung Electronics and SK hynix, the market’s two leading chip stocks, dropped 4.39 percent and 4.52 percent, respectively, dragging KOSPI lower.
The revenue gap, however, reflected different accounting methods rather than a drop in sales.
why_it_matters_hint: A market that led the AI trade is falling even after record earnings from its biggest company, a sign investors are asking how long the chip boom lasts.
notes: Follow-up of the Bloomberg report on Korea's fading AI trade in our 11 Oct 2026 edition (1011:C07-01). Analysts differ on the cause.
